haiku-low.q1: Held 10 minutes. If not claimed in time, Inventory's timer marks it EXPIRED and the stock goes back on sale; the claim is then refused.
haiku-low.q2: Stock is reserved before the charge. If any line is short, nothing is reserved, short items are returned, status is REJECTED_OUT_OF_STOCK, and Payment is never called.
haiku-low.q3: The order id is the idempotency key. A repeat charge call for the same order is treated as the same payment, and the provider is asked with that same key.
haiku-low.q4: Order is set CANCELLED_OUT_OF_STOCK, RefundRequested is published for a full refund, and the customer is emailed that it is out of stock with refund on the way.
haiku-low.q5: Cart is emptied only by the OrderConfirmed handler in Cart, after confirmation. A failed checkout leaves the cart unchanged so the customer can try again.
haiku-low.q6: Order is the coordinator that decides the next step. Its own database records each order's status, such as PENDING or AWAITING_PAYMENT.
haiku-low.q7: The provider sends a webhook to Payment, which stores the outcome and publishes PaymentSucceeded or PaymentDeclined on the broker. Order consumes that event.
haiku-low.q8: Payment inserts the provider event id under a unique constraint in the same transaction. A duplicate insert fails, so Payment replies 200 and publishes nothing. Order also updates only when status matches.
haiku-low.q9: On PaymentDeclined, Order sets PAYMENT_FAILED and publishes OrderFailed. Inventory consumes OrderFailed and releases the hold at once.
haiku-low.q10: Inventory's claim checks in one transaction that the hold is HELD and not past expires_at. If yes, the order is confirmed; if no, it is a late success and gets refunded and cancelled.
haiku-low.q11: The record becomes RETRYING with attempt count and last error. Payment's retry job re-runs it with backoff and never gives up, alerting a person after N failures. It is tracked in Payment's refunds table.
haiku-low.q12: The OrderConfirmed event causes Cart's OrderConfirmed handler to empty the cart named in it. Cart is the only service that does this.

sonnet.q1: Held 10 minutes (expires_at set 10 min ahead). If unclaimed, the Inventory timer (every minute) marks HELD holds past 10 min as EXPIRED and the stock goes back on sale. A claim after expiry is refused even if the timer hasn't run yet.
sonnet.q2: Before. Stock is reserved first, then Payment is asked to charge. Reservation is all lines or none in one transaction; if any line is short, nothing is reserved, short items are returned, order becomes REJECTED_OUT_OF_STOCK, the customer is told which items are short, and Payment is never called.
sonnet.q3: The idempotency key, which is the order id, is sent with the provider charge request and retries use the same key. Also, a repeat charge call for the same order is treated as the same payment, and only one open order per cart id exists.
sonnet.q4: The claim is refused, so Order sets CANCELLED_OUT_OF_STOCK, publishes RefundRequested and OrderFailed, and emails the customer (out of stock, full refund on the way). Payment refunds the full amount.
sonnet.q5: The cart is emptied only when OrderConfirmed is handled, by Cart. On every failure path the cart is left unchanged and the customer can try again.
sonnet.q6: The Order service is the coordinator that decides what happens next. The record of progress is the order status stored in Order's own database (PENDING, AWAITING_PAYMENT, CONFIRMED, etc.).
sonnet.q7: The provider calls a webhook on Payment (it talks only to Payment). Payment finds the payment by provider reference, stores the outcome and publishes a PaymentSucceeded or PaymentDeclined event via its outbox and relay to the broker, which Order consumes. A Payment timer polling the provider status can also supply a definite outcome.
sonnet.q8: Webhooks: in one transaction Payment inserts the provider event id (unique constraint) with the outcome; if the insert fails it replies 200 and does nothing. Events: consumers are safe to run twice; Order updates only if status is the expected one (AWAITING_PAYMENT), repeats in CONFIRMED or CANCELLED_OUT_OF_STOCK do nothing; claim and release are idempotent per order id; refund record is one per order id.
sonnet.q9: The hold is released (stock goes back on sale) at once. Payment publishes PaymentDeclined; Order, if AWAITING_PAYMENT, sets PAYMENT_FAILED and publishes OrderFailed; Inventory releases the hold on OrderFailed.
sonnet.q10: Order asks Inventory to claim. Inventory checks in one transaction whether the hold is still HELD and not past expires_at. If yes, hold becomes CLAIMED and the order is CONFIRMED; if no, the claim is refused and the order is cancelled as out of stock with a full refund. Even if the stock is still free, a lapsed hold still fails and is refunded.
sonnet.q11: The refund record becomes RETRYING with attempt count and last error. Payment's retry job re-runs due REQUESTED or RETRYING records with backoff, never gives up, and after N failures alerts a person. The pending refund is tracked in Payment's own database refunds table (refund record with status, attempts, last error, next attempt time).
sonnet.q12: The OrderConfirmed event (published by Order with the cart id when the order is CONFIRMED) causes it; the Cart service empties the cart named in the event.
